title: Artificial Intelligence
hosting_unit: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, College of Engineering
overview: A 22-credit AI minor for eligible MSU bachelor students, with programming foundations, algorithms, AI and a choice of advanced topics. Current course enrollment restrictions have not been reconciled with minor eligibility; the requirement inventory is therefore partial.

outcomes.text: Develop an interdisciplinary AI foundation for industry, government or further graduate study.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming I
courses.description: Introduces Python programming and program design, testing and problem solving.
courses.prerequisites: (LB 118 or concurrently) or (MTH 124 or concurrently) or (MTH 132 or concurrently) or (MTH 152H or concurrently)

courses.name: Introduction to Programming II
courses.description: Develops C++ programming, abstraction and fundamental data structures.
courses.prerequisites: (CSE 231 or CMSE 202) and (LB 118 or MTH 124 or MTH 132 or MTH 152H)

courses.name: Discrete Structures in Computer Science
courses.description: Studies logic, proofs, counting, relations and discrete structures used in computing.
courses.prerequisites: MTH 124 or MTH 132 or MTH 152H or LB 118

courses.name: Social, Ethical, and Professional Issues in Computing
courses.description: Examines professional judgment, legal and ethical responsibilities and the social effects of computing.
courses.prerequisites: CSE 232. Enrollment restrictions: Open to students in the Computational Data Science Major or in the Computer Science Major or in the Computer Science Minor or in the Lyman Briggs Computer Science Coordinate Major.

courses.name: Algorithms and Data Structures
courses.description: Designs, analyzes and applies fundamental algorithms and data structures.
courses.prerequisites: (CSE 232) and (CSE 260 or CMSE 202). Enrollment restrictions: Open to students in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering or in the Computer Engineering Major or in the Lyman Briggs Computer Science Coordinate Major or in the Lyman Briggs Data Science Coordinate Major or in the Data Science Major and open to juniors or seniors in the College of Engineering.

courses.name: Biometrics and Pattern Recognition
courses.description: Studies feature extraction and matching for face, fingerprint and iris recognition.
courses.prerequisites: (CSE 331) and (STT 351 or STT 380 or STT 430 or STT 441) and (MTH 314 or MTH 317H) and (MTH 234 or MTH 254H or LB 220). Enrollment restrictions: Open to juniors or seniors in the College of Engineering or in the Lyman Briggs Computer Science Coordinate Major or in the Lyman Briggs Computer Science Major or in the Computer Science Minor or in the Lyman Briggs Data Science Coordinate Major or in the Data Science Major.

courses.name: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: Develops machine-learning models and implements learning algorithms.
courses.prerequisites: (CSE 331) and (STT 351 or STT 380 or STT 430 or STT 441) and (MTH 314 or MTH 317H). Enrollment restrictions: Open to juniors or seniors in the College of Engineering or in the Lyman Briggs Computer Science Coordinate Major or in the Lyman Briggs Computer Science Major or in the Computer Science Minor or in the Data Science Major or in the Lyman Briggs Data Science Coordinate Major.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies advanced methods and algorithms for artificial intelligence.
courses.prerequisites: (CSE 331) and (MTH 314 or ECE 280 or MTH 317H). Enrollment restrictions: Open to juniors or seniors in the College of Engineering or in the Lyman Briggs Computer Science Coordinate Major or in the Computer Science Minor or in the Lyman Briggs Data Science Coordinate Major or in the Data Science Major.

requirements.title: Application and entrance grades
requirements.summary: Apply to Computer Science and Engineering. CSE 231 and CSE 260 each require at least 3.0 for acceptance; enrollment may be limited.

requirements.title: Eligible bachelor students and exclusions
requirements.summary: Available to MSU bachelor students except CS, Computer Engineering, Computational Data Science and Data Science BS students; unavailable with the CS minor.

requirements.title: Bachelor-degree overlap approval
requirements.summary: Minor courses may also satisfy the bachelor's degree with approval from the administering department and college.

requirements.title: Implied Calculus I preparation
requirements.summary: Calculus I is an implied component because it is a prerequisite for a required minor course. No course code or added credits are specified here.

requirements.title: University minor relationship and credit policy
requirements.summary: A minor accompanies the primary undergraduate degree and is unavailable with a same-named major. University minimum is 15 credits; this program's published minimum governs. Any required unique credits must be explicitly identified in the catalog and cannot also satisfy university, college or major requirements.

notes: The local minor curriculum and general minor policies are mapped, but the inventory is partial because current course enrollment restrictions conflict with the published minor audience.

CSE 231 and CSE 260 are both required minor courses and entrance conditions; their credits appear once. Each requires at least 3.0 for acceptance. Calculus I is implied preparation; no extra course code or credit is invented.

Catalog credit values are preserved with credit_unit unknown until institutional credit-system normalization is verified. Eight course descriptions and prerequisite/restriction observations are now reviewed; remaining course metadata and public resources remain unverified.
Local overlap is allowed only with degree-department and college approval; no unstated unique-credit minimum is invented. The university says any such minimum must be explicit in the catalog.
Catalog edition, calendar and launch date remain unverified. Institution-wide program coverage is not claimed.

Current open-ended course versions were read through the public course search and eight observed View all versions links. Historical versions in those pages are not treated as current. The minor excludes CS/CE/Computational Data Science/Data Science majors and the CS minor, yet required CSE 300 lists only Computational Data Science, Computer Science, Computer Science Minor and Lyman Briggs Computer Science Coordinate students. CSE 345 similarly omits the AI minor from its listed eligible programs; several electives restrict enrollment as well. No AI-minor exception was found in the reviewed sources, so eligibility remains unresolved and inventory is partial. Course 300 and 345 titles differ between minor table and course search; requirement-table titles remain unchanged. Published Credits remain unnormalized. CSE 345/434/446 and MTH 483 were visible in normal browser search, but their metadata is not automated in this bounded batch; their existing unknown fields remain null.
